## FLUX 3 instruction edit

One image in, one written instruction, one call: name the thing to change precisely enough that only one element matches, say what it becomes, and say what stays.

`aspect_ratio` is **auto**, so the edit keeps the input's frame. `resolution` is **match_input**: the output keeps the input's own size, shrunk to 4 MP if it is larger. Set a ratio only when the edit should change the frame, and say in the prompt what fills the new space.

You do not need a box for a single edit — FLUX 3 expands the instruction and often finds and boxes the element itself. Read `expanded_prompt` to see what it decided. If it picked the wrong thing, copy the rows from there into **flux3-box-edit** and correct them.

Colours land better as hex codes: *change only the middle bird to #e01075*.

`variation` is not sent to the API — flux-3-image has no seed. It is **fixed** here so a rerun with nothing changed costs nothing; bump it (or set it to *randomize*) for a fresh take. `expanded_prompt` is `result.prompt`, the prompt the model actually used after expanding yours.

## The prompt lives in one node

The **Shared Prompt** node feeds the prompt in this graph, so there is one
place to edit it. It emits a plain string, **not** a list. That is the difference between it and **Prompt
List**, which would make each node it feeds run once per line and multiply what the graph
costs.
